title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Medicare Levy and Medicare Levy Surcharge) Bill 2019
short_title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Medicare Levy and Medicare Levy Surcharge) Bill 2019

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would raise Medicare levy and surcharge low-income thresholds, including higher thresholds for eligible seniors and pensioners and additional amounts for dependent children.
It would increase individual and family exemption levels and related phase-in limits in line with consumer price movements, including the surcharge threshold for relevant family members.
The amendments would begin the day after royal assent and apply retrospectively to assessments for the 2018-19 income year and later income years.
changes: The ordinary individual low-income threshold would rise from $21,980 to $22,398.
The ordinary family threshold would rise to $37,794, plus $3,471 for each dependent child or student.
Eligible seniors’ and pensioners’ thresholds would become $35,418 for individuals and $49,304 for families.
The ordinary individual levy phase-in limit would rise to $27,997.
summary.affected: Low-income individuals and families, eligible seniors and pensioners, taxpayers with dependants and family members subject to the Medicare levy surcharge are affected.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Leigh
speeches.brief: Labor supported the Treasury Laws Amendment (Medicare Levy and Medicare Levy Surcharge) Bill 2019, which raises Medicare levy low-income thresholds in line with CPI for 2018-19. The party also criticised the government for hospital funding cuts, citing $715 million in current cuts and a $3 billion Medicare rebate freeze, and proposed a $2.8 billion Better Hospitals Fund.

speeches.speaker: Stuart Robert
speeches.brief: The Treasury Laws Amendment (Medicare Levy and Medicare Levy Surcharge) Bill 2019 increases Medicare levy low-income thresholds for singles, families, seniors and pensioners in line with CPI. For 2018-19, no Medicare levy is payable for singles earning up to $22,398, and for eligible single seniors and pensioners up to $35,418, with further thresholds for couples and families.
